body: To be honest, I first decided that Seema Malakaya Temple is one of the “components” of the Gangaramaiya temple complex. Only carried from the sacred "core" to the smoothing of Lake Beira. But as it turns out, Gangarama Sima Malaka is a Buddhist religious building in its own right. True, as the more advanced Srilankophiles argue, this sakral is mostly used by believers for meditation and recreation, not for worshipping the Buddha and other divine beings of the Buddhist pantheon. The history of this unusual temple dates back to the 19th century (however, I could not find even an approximate date of its appearance). It was erected directly on the lake and surrounded on all sides by Beira water. But over the years, the structure began to sink underwater - whether there was initially some construction error or the underwater "base" of the sacrala was simply dilapidated. So in 1976, designed by the architect Geoffrey Manning Bawa, a recognized authority on so-called tropical modernism, left his mark on the urban landscape of India, Singapore, Fiji, Mauritius, Indonesia and, of course, Sri Lanka. One of the creative features of Mr. Bawa was that his work was largely influenced by the colonial and traditional architecture of Ceylon. Architect played a huge role in his work, but denied imposing pre-defined forms and was not very "friends" with orthodox religiosity. Seema Malakaya Temple was renovated by a Sri Lankan Muslim non-business family, the Musaji, who expressed their desire to finance the construction of a virtual new temple in memory of their son. As for the architectural style of sakral: I am not a specialist in Buddhist temples in general and lake temples – in particular, but more advanced gurus of Buddhist temple-making claim that when Sima Malaka was built, the architect was inspired by the architecture of the ancient monastic city of Anuradhapura and the ancient Buddhist monastery on Mount Ritigala. Seema Malakaya Temple is based on three platforms raised above the water, which are connected to each other and to land by pontoon bridges. The object is super-original, unusual, interesting, so I recommend it unequivocally!!!
title: Seema Malakaya Temple: my first Asian LAKE Temple

body: This temple , standing on the waters of Lake Beira, is considered one of the most peaceful places in Colombo , where it is good to meditate people of all religions. During our own trip to Colombo, the driver of the rented car named this temple Gangaramai, but Sima Malaka is part of a famous Buddhist temple dedicated to recreation and meditation.The old temple of the late 19th century was almost submerged in 1975, and the city authorities trusted architect Geoffrey Bawa to build a new temple.The money for the construction was provided by a private individual in memory of his deceased son. The temple is built on three platforms connected to the shore by a pontoon bridge. At the entrance, business boys immediately demand 400 rupees for entry and strictly ensure that visitors remember to remove their shoes. All platforms have statues of the seated Buddha depicting various wise men. Vishnu, Shiva and Guanin sculptures rise above the Buddhas. Beneath the sacred tree, Bodhi is another Buddha statue near which worshippers pray and meditate. The young monk tries to communicate with tourists, but did not tie the sai-shin ropes on his wrist.I found the temple boring and uninteresting, probably because during her travels in Southeast Asia she saw temples more majestic and memorable.I guess if she had not visited, she would not have been upset.Or maybe I did not touch the Buddhist nirvana?

body: Seema Malakaya temple is in Central Colombo, in the middle of the Beira Lake. Though listed separately in TripAdvisor, Seema Malakaya is part of the nearby Gangarama temple. It had initially been built as a ritual house (also called chapter house) for buddhist priests where junior priests are ordained as senior priests and where rules of Sangha (buddhist priests) are implemented and disciplinary decisions taken and enforced.The original “Seema Malakaya” or chapter house started disintegrating in the seventies sinking into Beira lake. It was reconstructed in the late seventies to a modern design by the famous architect Geoffrey Bawa. It is a place for meditation and a gathering hall. The temple is on three platforms interconnected by pontoon bridges. The connection to James Peiris Mawatha too is via a pontoon bridge. The wood panelled central house of meditation is where one can sit and meditate or simply enjoy the scenic view surrounding the lake. Surrounding the central building are gold coloured seated buddha statues. On the four outer corners are statues of Hindu deities including Shiva and Ganesh. On the left platform is the bodhi tree and a seated Buddha statue flanked by two standing statues. The third platform on the right is the real “Seema Malakaya” with entry restricted to priests. I understand that this building also contains some valuable Buddhist books.Compared to the gaudy coloured Gangarama temple, this Seema Malakaya is simple, charming, attractive, and pleasant to the eye. I felt serene and tranquil after my visit.As with all temples in Sri Lanka – it is open to people of all faiths. The entrance ticket (required only by foreigners) to close-by Gangarama temple provides access to this Seema Malakaya too. Visitors are required to dress modestly and remove footwear at the entrance.
title: A Serene and Tranquil Sanctuary for Meditation

body: A magnificent example of Sri Lankan traditional architecture, which is a part of Gangaramaya situated in the middle of Beira lake. It is only few meters from Gangaramaya to this location. This is used for "Uposatha Karma" which is a deciplinary practice comes in Buddhism and meditation. If you are visiting this place you have to take off your shoes and hats. Your dress should be somewhat appropriate. It is opened for public on daily basis. When considering its history, the original buildings was constructed in late 19th century. But the constitution slowly sank in to waters. This pavilion was designed by famous architect Geoffrey Bawa. The wooden pavilion was raised on platform over the water. The roof consists of blue tiles. Around the main pavilion there are numerous seated buddha statue with different hand gestures. The neighboring platform consists of a Bodhi tree which is known as a sapling of Sri Maha Bodhi in Anuradhapura, a bell shaped stupa and a replica of Gal vihara standing buddha statue.
title: An edifice in the Beira lake

body: This is a Buddhist temple in Colombo, right next to Gangaramaya temple and is mainly used for meditation and rest, rather than for worship. The temple is constructed on three platforms over water (Beira Lake) and is connected to the mainland and with each other by bridges. All three platforms have numerous seated Buddha statues displaying different mudras. The main (central) platform houses wooden paneled shelter for meditation. On one of the side platforms is the Bodhi Tree. The four corners of the side platform have small temples dedicated to several Hindu deities like Shiva, Vishnu and Ganesha. A must visit if you are in interested in Buddhist culture and history.

It's not expensive, and keep it, as it allows you to visit the Gangaramaya Temple which is about 400 meters close.It's nice to walk around the temple and admire the golden buddhas that surround the temple and overlook the lake. body: More than the temple itself which is just a fairly moderate-sized pavilion with a smaller pavilion on one side and a cone-shaped chedi structure of a medium height (about 20 feet tall) on the other side, I was attracted (or even intrigued) by the "intensely" green water surrounding the temple, namely the water of Beira Lake that the temple is in (a short bridge connects the temple's main pavilion with the land side, and the left & right sides are also likewise connected with the main pavilion although they're much closer to the main pavilion compared to the distance between the main pavilion and the land side); and the medium-sized Buddha statues lined up on top of the short walls on all four sides of the pavilion grounds (with all of them facing the pavilion) also make an impressive sight for some nice photos especially at the back of the pavilion where, besides the statues, you also have a backdrop of some high rise buildings across the lake.Apart from the statues around, there are two "pretty long" elephant tusks on the sides of the "main Buddha" inside the pavilion and a fairly big Buddha statue under the tree in the open area on one side (where the chedi structure is) where there's also some pink statue made interesting by its multiple faces & multiple hands.Nearby, just a few minutes' walk to the north (a left turn after coming out of the Temple) is a little island with a park and a round-shaped pavilion on it connected to the land side by a nice pedestrian bridge (a lot better one than a small boardwalk-like bridge that connects to the Temple) and just a few minutes' walk to the east (cross the road in front of the Temple, turn right then left short after) is a much bigger temple called Gangaramaya with rows of Buddha statues (each row higher than the one in front) in the back and also like a museum inside.From the Kollupitiya Junction roundabout on Galle Rd.(with a big market on one corner), it's just about a 15-minute walk to this temple (a right turn from Galle Rd. at the roundabout if you're coming from the south, then a left turn after about 10 minutes, and you'll see the Temple on your left after about 5 minutes). Also by the way, Galle Face Green (the "lively" seaside promenade with food & drink vendors in green tents lined up on one side) is just about a 10-minute walk if you go straight on Galle Rd. past the Junction instead of turning right to get to this temple (I suggest you come back out onto Galle Rd. after the two temples, meaning this one & Gangaramaya, and continue on to Galle Face).

body: I used to visit here every weekend for it gave me a great spiritual feeling. You should go there during Wesak festival to see the gorgeous decors. But during that period the place will be crowded. However, if you're looking for a serene place to sit down for a few hours and maybe meditate around Colombo, this is the best place.

body: There's actually little to see as it's a small temple in the middle of a lake, but what a serene and peaceful place to worship. Otherwise, it's a great place for picture perfect photo ops.The entrance fee also allows entry into Gangaramaya Temple, so keep the ticket.
title: Picture perfect

body: Favorite religious hangout on a non festival day. You can awaken your spiritual part minus the ritualistic mayhem in the main temples.
title: Serene silence

body: Its a unique kind of meditation center in the middle of the pond. Nice place to visit.The only thing is the guard at the entrance was charging us some money. I have never seen a temple charging for the entry of visitors. The was no board or anything that states we have to pay to enter. When i said I would rather not visit if I have to pay 200LKR per person, then that man started bargaining and asked me to pay 200LKR for all the three people. I found it fraud.I think there are different ways to earn money from the tourist. So beware. Dont pay for any entry unless you see a proper board and get a receipt.
title: Nice

body: Nice location. There is a bridge near by too and some boat ride. Famous Garden and other tourist attractions in few kms area. Entrance fees applies and no public toilet, eating places around.
title: Good place for some snap shot in the city center.

body: We were not allowed to enter the premises and one person wanted us to pay Rs. 200/per person to take phograph of temple or enter it. No money was being demandedfrom locals.Devender BialaDelhi.
title: Entry Fee.

body: A beautiful small temple for meditation, situated in side Lake Beira in the center of Colombo. You can easily recognize it by the blue tiled roof. A series of Buddha statues flanks the temple ground; a serene place in a busy city. The architect of the temple is the famous Geoffrey Bawa. Sometimes there is a table with a middle age gentleman at the entrance of the temple, asking for an entrance fee, which is quite extraordinary, because usually this temple is free admittance. I didn't trust the intentions of this man.
title: Seema Malaka Temple, a beacon of rest

body: I've visited this beauful temple and spend couple minutes there. Just on my way out, the guy stopped me asking me to pay for a ticket. No where was written that visiors are obliged to pay for entering temple. It looked like he was self-hired and trying to get money from tourist. After that group of young Sri Lankan people told me that this temple is free to enter. This incident spoil my whole experience. In all, it looks that sacred places are bussines more than spiritual thing in Sri Lanka. It's shame and pitty.

body: This is an excellent place to come to if you want to get away from the hustle and bustle of the city around you. its right on the south Beria lake. please take care to be respectful of your surroundings as it is a Buddhist shrine as well as a little tranquil retreat.

There is a path way around the lake and a bridge let you go a small park in the middle of the lake, very nice place to make some walk and rest.
title: By other name Floating Temple!

body: This floating temple in the middle of the Beira Lake can be seen from Sir James Peiris road and is a tranquil place to inspire meditation.Bus 101 will pass in front of this temple. There is a bridge near this temple which take to small park, famous for love birds !
title: Iconic temple of Colombo

body: By far my favourite tourist spot in Colombo. The setting of this beautiful temple in the middle of Beira Lake is so serene. The moment we stepped on it's aisle leading to the temple with bronze buddha statues surrounding the holy abode, something so peaceful welcomed us and made us feel very much in an inexplicable bliss. It must be the cooling breeze or the view of the calm ducks or the leaves of the bodi trees swaying, but definitely do not miss this place, I tell you! Within walking distance to Gangaramayana Temple.
title: A peaceful retreat in the busy city!

body: This Temple is in the city centre in the lake.A very pretty well designed Temple. Ideal place to visit in the mornings or in the evenings.

body: An afternoon visit under a blazing sun is definitely not on . It is harsh on the senses and awful for aesthetic photography . If you have no choice , at least wear a thick pair of socks as the walkways are searing hot .
title: Avoid sunny afternoons

body: This small temple in the lake is a few minutes walk from Gangaramaya Temple and is included in the ticket. It's well worth taking time to stop there, too. The setting is lovely and the statues are interesting.
title: Same ticket as Gangaramaya Temple

body: There's not much to see but what is there is absolutely beautiful and well worth a half-hour visit..
title: Beautiful tranquil temple on the lake

body: One of the places that you have to visit if you are in Colombo ... In the middle of the Beira lake, it gives a magical feeling once you are inside the Seema-Malakaya. You can see the excellent craftsmanship with the statues and I recommend even non-Buddhists to visit the place just to get the feeling. Anyway the sound of the vehicles and the odour from the lake spoils the feeling...
title: Magical feeling can be Spoiled !!!

body: I visited the Seema Malakaya temple which is part of the Gangaramaya Temple and is also a centre for meditation. It surely is a very attractive temple and its beauty is amplified as its built on an artificial man made island by the tree lined lake. I gained access to the religious complex by walking over a pontoon board-walk. On the top of the enclosure boundary wall are numerous statues of Buddha sitting in different poses.Though its in the heart of Colombo, the calm of being on water did not let the hustle and bustle of the city affect me. The is no fee for the attraction but a donation of LKR 200 is appreciated. You will be given a receipt for the donation that you can show at the Gangaramaya Temple and hence wont have to pay anything there
title: Stop walking, Sit down and Relax

body: Across the road from Gangaramaya Buddhist Temple and the fee to get in covers entry into Gangaramaya too. Cost about 200 SLRupees but so worth it for both temples. Its on stilts in a lake which makes it so serene and the buddha statues surrounding it are beautiful against the backdrop.
title: Worth the entry fee as its coupled with Gangaramaya

body: On three island podiums on Beira Lake, Colombo easily visible from Sir James Peiris Road, is the Seema Malaka, a Buddhist temple, a beautiful & unexpected site. Amidst the hustle & bustle of the city, the tranquil temple takes us by surprise. Not to be outdone, we take to the bridge like walkway leading to the temple in the middle of the lake with the breeze cutting into us. Set on three linked platforms rising out of the lake, the temple has a small Bo tree & delicately carved kiosk on the two outer platforms standing on either side of the larger central structure. The lake is surrounded by fine old trees, provides welcoming breezes throughout the day & attracts pelicans, egrets & cormorants
title: Seema Malaka

(although i am a sri lankan)

body: You can reach it easily in the middle of a small lake. A modest but very nicely done temple with a lot of Buddha statues. Right next to it, there is an island that you can get to over a hanging bridge. Here you can find a great number of pelicans in the water and in the trees surrounding the lake. Also it´s very nice to meet all the Sri Lankan couples here, who sit around on benches everywhere, holding hands and enjoying a little twosome-time. A very common behavior in parks and such, as it´s not normal to do that on the streets or even in regular public places, so couples go into "semi-hiding". For westerners kind of funny to watch and experience.
title: Tranquility in the middle of a bustling metropole.

body: Just 2 km s from city center you can go to Seema Malaka Temple or Gangarama Temple. This is the place where they conduct Nawam Maha Perahara. A cultural event which takes place in Colombo annually . Gangarama Temple boasts for a huge museum, Antique Mercedes Benz cars etc.
title: Gangarama Temple

body: My wife and I were married here in May 2014. Despite it being short notice a relative with links to Gangarama Temple across the road made a request on behalf of us. The head priest invited us to meet with him and he immediately gave us his blessing and arranged for three priests to be present on the day to chant Pirith and bless us.The evening before we transported enough chairs from the main temple to Seema Malaka under the supervision of the site manager (a senoir member of the congregation). On the morning of the service, we were able to set up the lamp, decorations and food without problem.All in all we had a fantastic day. Despite the busy main road 100 yds from the temple, the noise is not a problem and it really is quite peaceful on the lake. Everyone remarked what a jewel the temple was in the middle of Colombo city.Despite there being no official charge for the services of the priests, it is customary to give a generous donation to the temple. This goes towards the upkeep of the temple and the lovely priests and monks within.
title: Perfection

body: This gem designed by Geoffrey Bawa (whose other works in Sri Lanka should be sought out) and beautifully set in a lake makes a very nice combination with the hodgepodge of the Gangaramaya Temple just a few blocks away. A very good lesson in the difference between spiritually advanced design and religious vulgarity.
title: A Lesson in Beautiful Design

body: Right in the middle of the Beira Lake sits this small but impressive temple that is a true oasis set far from the city and offering beautiful views and peaceful air. Loved every time I could spend at the place and it is a delight to be present at the place with the chants and ceremonies happening. Undoubtedly the main impact of the place comes from the location of the temple, The Lake.

body: When an older temple sank into the lake, a new one was designed by Geoffrey Bawa. It is small on several platforms in the lake. Strangely it is not identified on some maps of Colombo and some tuk-tuk drivers and others we consulted for directions did not know it. But it is worth a visit and it is only 2 blocks from the large Gangaramaya Buddhist Temple and museum, which is also worth visiting.

body: This is the meditation centre for Gangaramaya Temple. I went at night and it was beautifully lit up. A rain storm kept me there a while which was good as I could sit quietly and also interact with a local person who lived nearby and kindly gave me a stool to sit on. I was surprised at how my mind settled despite being in the middle of the busy city all lit up round me and it is surprisingly peaceful and conducive to settling the mind so I would really recommend some time here. Please, please can I ask you if you are a foreign tourist do not take photographs of yourself in front of the Buddha statues. I learnt in conversation that it really upsets the Sri Lankans. I read in the paper on my return that in some places it will not be tolerated and you could be arrested. They were more tolerant here as I saw some foreign people arrive and come in and take a picture in front of the big Buddha and leave but it prompted the local man to explain to me it is not seen as respectful behaviour.

title: beautiful shrine on water

body: This little temple is on an island in South Beira Lake. The neighbourhood is noisy and chaotic. A main road passes right by. Still it seems as soon as you step across the bridge you're in another world. It is nicely lit at night so you can get some dramatic photos. They lock the doors at 9:00 pm.It is not so much a temple as a place to meditate. It may seem like just another tourist attraction, but it is a Buddhist temple, so take your shows off and allow the people who are there to meditate some peace.

title: Unlike any other Buddhist temple
body: Designed by Bawa, this is a beautiful modern temple that is definitely worth visiting. Very simple and spare. Be sure to peek in at the Hindu shrines: several of the hindu gods were brought into Sri Lankan Buddhism, as also seen in the associated temples in Kandy. The temple also runs vocational classes in nearby buildings to teach trades and help people establish businesses and prosper.

title: Peaceful and interesting, although eventually anticlimactic experience
body: I had an afternoon to kill in Colombo, so this ended up on the itinerary. It was actually the most pleasant site I saw in Colombo, which is saying a lot, since I would not recommend that any tourist spend any time there if possible and instead head for the beach or highlands. The temple is calm and peaceful, and fairly clean. The view over the lake is serene. Best of all, I did not encounter a single tout or peddler of some sort. All in all, worth about 15 minutes of your time and a couple photos, as it is simply an open meditation-type space, and some nicely arranged statues, which is why I'm pegging it as a "poor" attraction. Avoid this place unless you have some real time to kill - as an alternative, any market visit or a brisk walk around the seafront in Colombo will be more interesting.

title: A change from many of the temples.
body: This temple, designed by Geoffrey Bawa, sits on a lake in Colombo's Slave Island area. It is well worth a visit if you are in the area, but probably not worth a major detour. The three islands are reached by a bridge and give a contemporary take on temple design. But all the usual temple elements are there: image room, stupa, statuary etcThe lake also has a pleasant island reached by a suspension bridge and the top end (North) of the lake has a nice, inexpensive outdoor cafe.

title: Lovely location over the lake, picturesque, peaceful.
body: This is a very small but beautiful temple built on platforms over a lake - great photo opportunities here, with a gold-and-white reclining Buddha, three separate sections with statues and a stupa. Pelicans on the lake and swan-shaped pedaloes for hire too.
